_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. This week’s question comes up every time the sky goes grey: will it actually rain, or is it just sulking? Most grey skies never drop a thing, and one kind nearly always does.

replies.say: Grey clouds mean rain, don’t they?
replies.back: Not as often as you’d think. That’s the lesson.

turns.them: Why some days the air bubbles up and some days it lies flat, the lid that spreads heaps into a grey sheet, and the one grey sky that soaks you. Questions at the end, as usual.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Photographs first, then some grey skies to call.
Good. Next lesson we climb higher and sort the whole sky.
